summary: Each of the three strongest solver-accepted breaking sites now uses one bounded two-skin aerated crest surface instead of a zero-thickness membrane. The skins share the same solver-shaped profile, separate only along the local profile normal, and join at the fully masked plunge boundary. A first visible-crown connector produced vertical slivers in the matched Zambezi capture and was rejected before release; the retained masked connector removes that artifact. The result adds subtle front-to-back parallax without changing physics, but it does not yet read as photoreal overturning whitewater.

zambezi_breaking_water_side.visual_verdict: Retain as a bounded technical candidate. The final frame has no crown-cap slivers, slab, dome, tent, rail, card, or shoreline regression. The added depth is subtle and does not close the missing volumetric aeration, hole, pile, recirculation, spray, or mist defects.

rejected_iteration.visible_crown_connector: Rejected before release because the matched Zambezi frame exposed repeated vertical dark or bright slivers along the cross-section. Moving the connection to the exactly zero-alpha plunge row removed the artifact while keeping each site's two skins in one connected procedural mesh.

validation.unreal_editor_build: SmokeEmIfYouGotEmEditor Mac Development succeeded after the final masked-connector source and native-test changes
validation.shared_water_and_runnable_maps: RaftSim.P2.WaterSurfaceRenders plus all six RaftSim.P4.RiverMapLoads completed 7/7 with zero failures; four succeeded cleanly and three succeeded with established warnings
validation.matched_renderer_capture: The Zambezi breaking-water-side frame completed at 1280x720 with the same command, camera contract, and eight-second delay as the exact-current baseline

remaining_photoreal_defects: The crest envelope remains a masked presentation surface rather than a genuinely resolved entrained-air volume with coherent overturn, pile, hole, and recirculation.
Spray, suspended droplets, mist, rock-contact plumes, raft wake, paddle interaction, wet fabric, and camera-lens water remain incomplete or unapproved.
The sampled live-water rise and rapid profile remain visibly smooth and analytical at close range.

Terrain, banks, boulders, vegetation, atmosphere, raft equipment, characters, anatomy, PPE, animation, and hand/paddle contact remain below the requested photoreal target in at least one runnable river.
No named guide, geospatial, hydraulic, environment-art, water-VFX, rights, hazard-readability, product, or target-platform reviewer has approved full-scene promotion.
required_external_acceptance_gates: A named whitewater water-VFX and environment-art reviewer must approve the foam, crest, hole, spray, mist, reflection, transmission, and shoreline-contact presentation across representative flow bands.
Qualified guides for the represented rivers must approve rapid identity, aeration placement, line and hazard readability, and raft/swimmer occlusion at the represented flows.
A geospatial or technical-art reviewer must approve source alignment and the labeled procedural terrain, bank, bathymetry, and rapid-geometry infill boundaries.
A rights and provenance reviewer must approve every production texture, mesh, reference-media use, attribution, and redistribution record.
A safety and gameplay-readability reviewer must approve that foam, spray, mist, vegetation, lighting, raft, and characters do not hide hazards, swimmers, rescue targets, or solver failures.
Target-platform qualification must pass desktop performance, memory, streaming, fresh-machine rendering, and required VR or low-power readability budgets.
The product owner must approve the integrated moving-camera river, raft, equipment, character, animation, and water interaction presentation before M9 or photoreal promotion.
